# Modernizing


Utility Payments


Article


NOV 24 2026


Michael Garvett


Head of Integrated Partnerships & Sales, Fiserv


## How an ISV built a customer engagement platform and achieved 75% customer adoption


For many utility providers, the customer payment experience has become an important part of how they serve their communities. Customers expect convenient ways to pay, clear communication and reliable digital tools. At the same time, utilities need systems that are dependable, easy to support and built for the long term.


[Central Service Association (CSA)](https://www.csa1.com/) understands these requirements well. The Tupelo, Mississippi-based company has served utilities for more than 80 years, providing systems and software that help small- and medium-sized utilities run their businesses.


Featured Video


Hear how Central Service Association (CSA) has partnered with Fiserv to provide systems and software that help small- and medium-sized utilities run their businesses.


Building a modern utility payments experience


In 2018, CSA set out to build a customer engagement and payments platform that could help its utility customers modernize how they serve their own customers. The goal was to create a solution that could help utilities better manage customer interactions and payment experiences, through technology they could count on. But building a platform that supports mission-critical utility payments required more than payment processing technology. CSA needed a partner that could support its business, its customers and its long-term growth.


After an extensive evaluation process, CSA selected Fiserv.


“We looked at all the major processors in the industry,” said Al Williams, senior vice president of strategic initiatives at CSA. “We decided on Fiserv because of the technology and the customer support we felt we were going to receive.”


With a mission-critical application like payment services, it’s really important that we have a partner that’s standing behind us.


Al Williams


Senior Vice President of Strategic Initiatives, CSA


Key differentiator: Tailored customer support


CSA’s customer relationships run deep. The company serves more than 100 utilities directly, and approximately 160 organizations when including subsidiary operations. Some customers have worked with the organization for decades, and all rely on the company not only for software but also for the support and service that help them operate confidently. When CSA needed a support approach that fit its business and its customers, Williams said Fiserv listened.


“We had some needs that were a little different in the support area, and Fiserv listened to us and really crafted a solution for support that was meant to work for us and our customers,” he said. “It’s worked out perfectly. It’s one of the reasons we’ve been able to grow it like we have.”


From zero adoption to more than 75%+


When CSA launched its platform, no customers were using the payment processing and customer engagement solution. Today, more than three-quarters have adopted it. A key contributor to that growth was the ability to move quickly without sacrificing the customer experience.


“It’s been a real success,” Williams said. “And we’ve been able to go as fast as we wanted to. Fiserv was there to make sure that the onboarding processes were done quickly and effectively.”


For software companies looking to embed payments into their platforms, that balance is critical. Growth is sustainable only if onboarding, support and day-to-day operations can keep pace.


Defining the partnership: Commitment


“We feel the Fiserv team is committed to what we are trying to achieve,” Williams said. “If we have needs, they take care of those needs in a timely fashion. We feel like they’re invested in our business.”


For CSA, that commitment shows up in the relationship with the account team and the responsiveness of support. It’s a simple point, but an important one: For software providers implementing embedded payments, the payments partner becomes part of the customer experience. The right partner can help create confidence; the wrong partner can create friction that becomes difficult to unwind.


What other software providers can learn from CSA


Williams has a clear message for other ISVs and software providers evaluating payment processing partners: Look at the full picture.


“It’s easy just to get focused on price,” he said. “It’s easy to get focused on one aspect or another. You’ve really got to take everything into account.”


Williams’ advice is to talk with other software providers, learn from their experiences and think beyond the immediate decision. “You have to think about what it’s going to be like seven years from now,” he said.


That long-term view is especially important for companies serving industries like utilities, where reliability, trust and continuity matter. A payments decision made today can shape the customer experience for years to come.


Choosing a payments partner for long-term growth


CSA’s journey shows what can happen when a software provider takes a long-term view and chooses a payments partner that can grow with the business.


For Williams, the value of that decision is clear.


“I can’t imagine having put three-quarters of our customers on a solution where we had problems, and where there was difficulty with our partner,” he said. “Fortunately, we had a really good partner, and they’ve been riding with us the whole way.”

Frequently Asked Questions


Learn more about modernizing utility payments


-


Why are payments an important part of the utility customer experience?


-


Payments are often one of the most frequent interactions customers have with their utility provider. A reliable, convenient payment experience can help improve customer satisfaction, reduce friction and support stronger customer engagement. For utilities, payments are also a mission-critical business function that requires dependable technology and support.


-


What should utility software providers look for in a payment processing partner?


-


Utility software providers should evaluate more than pricing alone. Key considerations include technology, onboarding capabilities, customer support, reliability and long-term scalability. CSA spent months evaluating payment processors before selecting a partner that could support both its business and its utility customers.


-


Why is customer support important when selecting a payment processor?


-


Payment services play a critical role in day-to-day operations. A strong support model can help software providers onboard customers efficiently, resolve issues quickly and maintain service reliability. Customer support was one of the key factors CSA evaluated when choosing a payments partner.


-


How can utility software companies drive adoption of digital payment solutions?


-


Successful adoption depends on more than technology. Effective onboarding, responsive support and a seamless customer experience can help encourage adoption over time. Since launching its customer engagement and payments platform, CSA has grown adoption to more than three-quarters of its customer base.


-


Why should businesses and organizations work with software platforms that offer integrated payments?


-


Integrated payments can help streamline operations, simplify the payment experience, reduce manual processes and create a more consistent customer journey. By embedding payments directly into the software experience, organizations can manage key workflows within a single platform.
